speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Blitzy, the autonomous software development platform built for enterprise scale.
zh: 本期节目由 Blitzy 赞助，这是一个为企业级规模打造的自主软件开发平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's code bases have grown beyond human comprehension.
zh: 如今的代码库已经超越了人类所能理解的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Millions of lines, decades of tech debt, and complexity existing tools just can't fathom.
zh: 数百万行代码、数十年的技术债，以及现有工具根本无法理解的复杂度。

speaker: Unknown
en: With Blitzy, thousands of specialized agents reverse engineer the code base, mapping the architecture, dependencies, and business logic.
zh: 借助 Blitzy，数千个专门的智能体会对代码库进行逆向工程，梳理架构、依赖关系和业务逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that context, the platform then autonomously executes entire epics, writing, validating, and testing the code for every project.
zh: 有了这些上下文，平台随后便可自主执行整个 epic,为每个项目编写、验证和测试代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: The result?
zh: 结果如何?

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortune 500 enterprises are able to modernize legacy systems and ship new features five times faster.
zh: 《财富》500 强企业得以现代化改造遗留系统，并以五倍的速度交付新功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Want to try Blitzy on your code today?
zh: 想今天就对你的代码试用 Blitzy 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Unlock 1 million lines of reverse engineering and 25K lines of code generation by visiting blitzy.com slash sandbox.
zh: 访问 blitzy.com/sandbox,即可解锁 100 万行逆向工程额度和 25K 行代码生成额度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've started to enter a phase of AI that's not just about making models smarter.
zh: 我们已经开始进入 AI 的一个新阶段，不再只是让模型更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also about making them economically sustainable.
zh: 还要让它们在经济上可持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: As reasoning models consume more tokens, context windows continue to grow.
zh: 随着推理模型消耗更多 token,上下文窗口持续增长，

speaker: Unknown
en: And agents become embedded in more products and workflows, the economics of these systems are becoming impossible to ignore.
zh: 而智能体被嵌入越来越多的产品和工作流中，这些系统的经济账正变得无法忽视。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's given rise to a new conversation around tokenomics, how we think about the costs, incentives, and trade-offs shaping the next generation of AI.
zh: 这催生了围绕 tokenomics(代币经济学)的新讨论，即我们该如何思考塑造下一代 AI 的成本、激励和权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: One person who's been thinking deeply about this is Stanford professor and Big Spin co-founder Chris Potts.
zh: 在这个问题上思考颇深的一位人士是斯坦福教授兼 Big Spin 联合创始人 Chris Potts。

speaker: Unknown
en: His recent work argues that measuring AI progress requires looking beyond model benchmarks to ask a different question.
zh: 他最近的工作主张，衡量 AI 的进步需要超越模型基准，去问一个不同的问题：

speaker: Unknown
en: What are our tokens actually buying us?
zh: 我们的 token 到底为我们买到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's Chris explaining how he thinks about tokenomics.
zh: 下面是 Chris 解释他对 tokenomics 的思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another interesting moment to be in as we're all being made aware of the true costs of all this AI usage.
zh: 这又是一个有趣的时代，因为我们都在被迫意识到所有这些 AI 使用的真实成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The analogy here is like it used to cost me $20 to take a ride share to the airport, Uber or Lyft, and now it costs $90.
zh: 这里的类比就像是，以前打个网约车去机场要花 20 美元，Uber 或 Lyft,现在要 90 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's more like $20 to like $500 or something, right?
zh: 但这更像是 20 美元涨到 500 美元或什么的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's happening is that the big providers are testing the waters on charging us.
zh: 我认为正在发生的事情是，大型提供商正在试探着向我们收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: The true costs, plus whatever profit they need to make as they all try to gear up for IPOs and so forth.
zh: 收取真实成本，加上他们需要赚取的利润，因为他们都在为 IPO 之类做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in turn, that is very quickly leading people to ask questions like, what is the return on investment for all these tokens that we have purchased?
zh: 反过来，这也很快让人们开始提出这样的问题：我们购买的这些 token 的投资回报率是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a very tricky area to be in because what does it mean to think about value in this context?
zh: 这是一个非常棘手的领域，因为在这种语境下，思考价值意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Sam Charrington, and this is the TwiML AI Podcast.
zh: 我是 Sam Charrington,这里是 TwiML AI 播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: For over a decade, I've been exploring the ideas and innovation shaping the future of AI through conversations like this one that help you understand what's real, what's next, and what matters.
zh: 十多年来，我一直通过像这样的对话，探索塑造 AI 未来的思想与创新，帮助你理解什么是真的、什么是下一个、什么是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's jump in.
zh: 让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to say thanks for coming on.
zh: 我要感谢你来做节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been looking forward to this conversation.
zh: 我一直很期待这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think where I'd love to start us off is to really dig into your background and how it kind of got you, you know, to where you are now.
zh: 我想我最希望的开场方式，是深入了解你的背景，以及它是如何让你走到今天的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, my background is in linguistics.
zh: 好的，我的背景是语言学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Linguistics proper, not even natural language processing.
zh: 是正宗的语言学，甚至不是自然语言处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did my PhD on, among many other things, swears.
zh: 我读博士时研究的诸多内容之一是脏话。

speaker: Unknown
en: What swears are like, why we swear, what information they encode, what kind of taboos exist around them and so forth.
zh: 脏话是什么样的、我们为什么说脏话、它们编码了什么信息、围绕它们存在什么样的禁忌，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was actually the trigger that got me into NLP because I wanted a lot of data of people swearing.
zh: 这实际上是把我带入 NLP 的触发点，因为我想要大量人们说脏话的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to know what the context was like, what their intentions were.
zh: 我想知道语境是什么样的，他们的意图是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I turned to corpora.
zh: 于是我转向了语料库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from there, you start using NLP toolkits to add structure to those corpora.
zh: 从那里开始，你开始使用 NLP 工具包来为这些语料库添加结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a few years, maybe you're writing your own tools for doing that work.
zh: 几年之后，也许你就在自己编写工具来做这些工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when you look back after 18 years or whatever it's been, you're just an AI person or an NLP person.
zh: 然后当你回顾这 18 年左右的时光，你就成了一个 AI 人或 NLP 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that is the true story.
zh: 但这才是真实的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like if I had to, I could trace the lineage of every one of my current projects back to my fascination with why we care when someone drops an F-bomb.
zh: 我觉得如果需要的话，我可以把我现在每一个项目的历史脉络都追溯到我对一件事的着迷：为什么有人在别人爆粗口时会在意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So are you an F-bomb dropper or did you come at it from the perspective of trying to understand these others?
zh: 那么你自己会说脏话吗，还是你是从试图理解这些人的角度切入的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think very infrequently in my life, for my linguistics class, Semantics and Pragmatics, which is about linguistic meaning, on the final day, we always do a class on swearing.
zh: 我想在我的人生中很少说。在我的语言学课程「语义学与语用学」——它研究语言意义——的最后一天，我们总会上一堂关于脏话的课。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I review the history and we kind of tie all the course themes together.
zh: 我会回顾脏话的历史，并把课程的所有主题串联起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: My handouts for that are full of swears.
zh: 我的讲义里满是脏话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I only swear once in the lecture.
zh: 但我在讲课中只说一次脏话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I present the result that people remember things better if the utterance contains a swear because it has a kind of emotional resonance, very primitive reaction.
zh: 我展示一个研究结果：如果话语中包含脏话，人们会记得更牢，因为它有一种情感共鸣，一种非常原始的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in that moment, I pick some fact from the course, some trivial thing, and I restate it with a swear.
zh: 所以在那一刻，我会从课程中挑一个事实，某个琐碎的东西，然后带上一句脏话把它重述一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I say, all of you will remember this for eternity.
zh: 然后我说，你们所有人都会永远记住这一刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other than that, I'm very shy about it in the class.
zh: 不过除了那次之外，我在课堂上对这件事很害羞。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's funny.
zh: 那很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure there is loads of research on this, but I grew up in New York City and as a New Yorker, I think that swearing is just kind of part of my natural language and way of communicating.
zh: 我确信这方面有大量研究，但我在纽约市长大，作为一个纽约人，我觉得说脏话基本上就是我自然语言和交流方式的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I married a Midwestern girl and she doesn't tolerate it at all.
zh: 而我娶了一个中西部女孩，她完全不能容忍说脏话。

speaker: Unknown
en: She doesn't do it.
zh: 她自己不说。

speaker: Unknown
en: She doesn't tolerate it.
zh: 她不能容忍它。

speaker: Unknown
en: She won't tolerate it for me.
zh: 她不容忍我说脏话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it made for, we've been married for 30 years, so I adapt quickly, apparently.
zh: 这就造成了，我们结婚已经30年了，所以显然我适应得很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it, you know, for a long time, it took a lot of restraint to, like, change that way of communicating, particularly when I'm communicating about something that I'm excited about or emotional about or, you know, want to convey the importance of.
zh: 但是，你知道，很长一段时间里，改变那种交流方式需要很大的克制，尤其是当我在谈论一些让我兴奋的事、有情绪的事，或者你知道，想要传达其重要性的事情时。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a really interesting topic.
zh: 这是一个非常有趣的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm
zh: 而我

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we're not going to turn the podcast into a podcast about swearing, but I imagine there's enough research there that we could if we wanted to.
zh: 好吧，我们不会把这个播客变成一个关于说脏话的播客，但我想那方面的研究足够多，如果我们想做的话是可以的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a fascinating area, yeah, because it gets right to the heart of the culture that we've constructed and how it relates to our usage and everything else about us.
zh: 这是一个很迷人的领域，是的，因为它直击我们所构建的文化核心，以及它如何与我们的语言使用和我们其他的一切相关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's fascinating that we have swears.
zh: 是的，我们有脏话这件事本身就很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: When the old swears lose their power, we invent new ones.
zh: 当旧的脏话失去力量时，我们就会发明新的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We pretend like nobody should use them.
zh: 我们假装没人应该使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you say, people use them all the time and it feels like an important part of being a language user that we've got them available to us.
zh: 但正如你所说，人们一直在使用它们，而且感觉这是我们作为语言使用者很重要的一部分，就是我们拥有它们可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Endless string of questions.
zh: 无穷无尽的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to hear your take on kind of a linguist in the age of modern AI, you know, transformers, statistical models, you know, this is a, NLP used to be kind of coming from a linguistic perspective and now the entire field is shifted to a statistical perspective.
zh: 我很想听听你作为现代 AI 时代的语言学家的看法，你知道，transformer、统计模型，你知道，这是一个——NLP 曾经某种程度上源自语言学视角，而现在整个领域已经转向了统计学视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd love to hear your reflections on
zh: 我很想听听你对这段经历的反思

speaker: Unknown
en: Being on the other side of that transition as well as maybe more importantly ways that you think that kind of the traditional foundational linguistics is still important to the way we think about AI today.
zh: 既包括作为那场转型的另一方的经历，也许更重要的是，你认为传统的、基础性的语言学在哪些方面对于我们今天思考 AI 的方式仍然重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: These questions are on my mind all the time.
zh: 这些问题一直萦绕在我心头。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because I operate at the intersection of all these different fields.
zh: 是的，因为我 operates 在所有这些不同领域的交叉点上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will say it's useful to distinguish in this context linguistics.
zh: 而我要说，在这个语境下区分语言学是有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people in my department at Stanford study language and social identity, historical linguistics, the structure of language.
zh: 我在斯坦福大学系里的同事们研究语言与社会身份、历史语言学、语言的结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're just doing scientific investigation of language as a human phenomenon.
zh: 他们只是在把语言作为一种人类现象进行科学研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they are not technologists and they're not trying to inform technology.
zh: 他们不是技术专家，也不试图为技术提供参考。

speaker: Unknown
en: So their project is interestingly impacted by technological developments.
zh: 所以他们的课题以一种有趣的方式受到技术发展的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: For NLP people who are of course participating directly in the engineering project, they're affected in a very different way by the rise of GenAI and the kind of homogeneous nature of the solutions that people now adopt in that space.
zh: 而对于那些当然直接参与工程项目的 NLP 从业者来说，GenAI 的兴起以及人们现在在这个领域所采用的那种同质化的解决方案，以一种非常不同的方式影响着他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for the linguists, I feel like this is the most exciting moment that anyone could have dreamed of.
zh: 所以对于语言学家来说，我觉得这是任何人所能梦想到的最激动人心的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel incredibly privileged to be alive in this moment where humans encounter for the very first time non-human creatures that use our language very fluently.
zh: 我感到无比荣幸能在这样一个时刻活着：人类第一次遇到能非常流利地使用我们语言的非人类生物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's weirding us all out.
zh: 我觉得这把我们所有人都搞得很不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from the point of view of understanding the human capacity for language, what a gift, because you can ask about the mechanisms, which are different from humans, but obviously sufficient for achieving a certain kind of behavioral performance.
zh: 但从理解人类语言能力的角度来看，这是多么好的礼物，因为你可以去探究那些机制，它们与人类不同，但显然足以实现某种行为表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can think about them as investigative tools.
zh: 我们可以把它们当作研究工具来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we train them on the internet.
zh: 我的意思是，我们用互联网训练它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're basically incredibly powerful distributional learners, and we can learn a lot from them about the true structure of language by just looking at the kinds of things that they learn.
zh: 它们基本上是极其强大的分布学习者，我们只需观察它们学到的东西，就能从中学到很多关于语言真实结构的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it really gets at the heart of core questions in linguistics about how much of language learning is innate and the nature of our capacity and whether it's statistical or symbolic.
zh: 这真正触及了语言学核心问题的本质：语言学习中有多少是天生的、我们这种能力的本质是什么、它是统计的还是符号的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All those things come flooding in in a completely fresh way.
zh: 所有这些问题都以一种全新的方式涌入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so whatever your reaction to language models is, it should be a significant one, right?
zh: 所以无论你对语言模型的反应是什么，它都应该是重大的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This should be causing you to rethink key questions.
zh: 这应该会促使你重新思考关键问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's all you could hope for as a scientist, that you have new angles, new perspectives, new questions reopened.
zh: 而作为一个科学家，这就是你所能期望的一切：你有了新的角度、新的视角、被重新打开的新问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's been incredible.
zh: 这一直令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: For NLP, I think it's a more uncertain prospect because...
zh: 对于 NLP 来说，我认为前景更不确定，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Pre the arrival of like pre-trained models, which for me would be like the ELMO model back in 2017, 2018.
zh: 在预训练模型出现之前，对我来说那大概是2017、2018年的 ELMO 模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before that, there was still a lot of statistical work, of course, and we were in the deep learning era.
zh: 在那之前，当然仍然有大量的统计学工作，我们处于深度学习时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you could still, for example, do a PhD that was entirely about some specific phenomenon and maybe some very specific tweak to a model.
zh: 但你仍然可以，比如说，做一个完全围绕某个特定现象、也许还有对某个模型某个非常具体调整的博士研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you could say, I'm going to work on summarization and I've got a new idea about how to do that well using deep learning models.
zh: 你可以说，我要做摘要方向的工作，而且我对如何用深度学习模型把它做好有了一个新想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: That could be your PhD.
zh: 那可以是你的博士论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we started to see 2018, 2019, 2020, especially with the arrival of GPT-3, that that was a very uncertain prospect because you might wake up one morning to find that you had been completely scooped.
zh: 我们在 2018、2019、2020 年开始看到的情况是,尤其是随着 GPT-3 的到来,那是一个前景非常不确定的时期,因为你可能某天早上醒来,发现自己的工作已经被彻底抢先了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That with essentially no effort, one of these large pre-training runs had done better than you at the thing that you'd worked so hard on.
zh: 也就是说,几乎不费吹灰之力,某一次大型预训练运行就在你辛苦钻研的那个问题上做得比你好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that caused an interesting, probably overall productive, but interesting and challenging crisis for people, especially students who are trying to figure out what to do next with their PhD research.
zh: 这引发了一场有趣的、总体上可能是有益的、但既有趣又艰难的危机,尤其是对那些正在思考自己的博士研究接下来该做什么的学生来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think all of us felt a kind of real uncertainty in that moment.
zh: 但我认为,在那一刻,我们所有人都感到一种真实的不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I remember the anxiety of that time and
zh: 是啊,我记得那个时候的焦虑,而且

speaker: Unknown
en: I always felt it was kind of expressed as, you know, is research in NLP fundamentally like scale limited or do you need a certain degree of scale that only a handful of organizations have to do foundational research?
zh: 我一直觉得这种焦虑大概可以表述为,你知道的,NLP 研究是不是从根本上受规模限制,还是说你需要只有少数几家公司才拥有的那种规模程度才能做基础研究?

speaker: Unknown
en: And is everyone else going to be relegated to like poking the, poking the beast and seeing what it does?
zh: 而其他所有人是不是都注定只能去戳一戳那头野兽,看看它会有什么反应?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious, do you feel like that was an anxiety that's passed or is it still very present?
zh: 我很好奇,你觉得那种焦虑已经过去了,还是依然非常现实地存在着?

speaker: Unknown
en: Has it panned out quite like that?
zh: 事情的走向是不是真的就是那样?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you, you know, how has it been resolved for you?
zh: 你怎么,你知道的,你最后是怎么看待这个问题的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Also fascinating, not resolved.
zh: 同样很吸引人,没有解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something I discuss a lot with my collaborators and with my students.
zh: 这是我经常和我的合作者以及我的学生讨论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all trying to figure this out in this moment.
zh: 我们现在都在试图弄清楚这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will say one concrete thing we did was orient a lot of our research toward interpretability.
zh: 我要说我们做的一件具体的事,就是把我们的很多研究转向了可解释性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the project of understanding how these models end up being so good at such hard tasks.
zh: 也就是去理解这些模型究竟是怎么做到在如此困难的任务上表现如此出色的。
